items.text: Take the PSAT/NMSQT in October to get a baseline score and check National Merit eligibility.
Confirm senior-year course selections reflect the strongest schedule Kyle can handle well, not just the most APs available.
Start a running log of activities, jobs, and leadership roles with dates, hours, and specific contributions - build it now instead of reconstructing it next fall.
Have a direct family conversation about what you're willing to spend, so “reach,” “match,” and “safety” include a financial-safety category from the start.
Set up a free profile on a couple of college search tools to explore options - this is research, not applying.
Decide between the SAT and ACT and register for a spring test date.
Visit a mix of campus types - large state school, small college, urban, suburban - before the college list gets built, so preferences come from real visits, not assumptions.
Run the Net Price Calculator on 3-5 schools spanning different selectivity and cost, to see real numbers instead of sticker price.
Narrow academic and career interests enough to shape the college list, without forcing Kyle to commit to a major.
Identify two junior-year teachers in core subjects who know Kyle's work well, as likely recommendation-letter writers.
Formally request recommendation letters before the school year ends - teachers get flooded with requests every fall.
Draft a first-pass college list sorted into reach, target, likely, and financial-safety tiers, with the criteria for each tier written down.
Take a second SAT/ACT sitting if the plan calls for one, and decide whether testing is finished.
Put together the resume or “brag sheet” the counselor and recommenders will use to write about Kyle.
Start brainstorming Common App personal essay topics - ideas only, not a draft yet.
Finalize the college list at roughly 8-12 schools spread across the reach/target/likely/safety tiers.
Visit the remaining priority campuses and note specific details worth using later in “why this school” essays.
Write a full draft of the Common App personal essay before senior year starts.
Open the Common App account (submissions can't go in before August 1) and start filling in the activities section.
Draft supplemental “why us” essays for any schools with early deadlines.
Take a final SAT/ACT sitting in August or September if another score jump is realistic.
Submit Early Action or Early Decision applications - most deadlines fall on November 1 or November 15.
Confirm every recommender and the school counselor have actually submitted their materials.
Submit Regular Decision applications on a rolling basis through the fall rather than all at once in December.

File the FAFSA as soon as it opens - the 2028-29 form (Kyle's cycle, for fall 2028 enrollment), expected to open around October 1, 2027. File within the first couple of weeks: some state grants and college aid are first-come, first-served, so waiting until winter costs real money.
Confirm every college on the list has received and processed the FAFSA, and respond quickly to any verification requests - don't just file it and assume it's done.
Complete the CSS Profile for any private colleges that require it.
Track and meet merit scholarship deadlines, which often land earlier than the admission deadline itself.
Compare financial aid offers using actual net cost once decisions arrive, not the headline sticker price.
